facts.text: Welsh folklore, not game canon: the Tylwyth Teg ('the fair family') are the fairies of Wales.
The ranger's brew and the fair folk's hospitality are Living Server writing.

story:
The Tylwyth Teg, the fair family, hunt the high woods of the Pennines and do not like to be seen, and the riders of the tops know them by their bows and by nothing else. Their rangers walk furthest from the rovers' woods, alone, and carry the family's brew in a horn at their belts.

The brew is the fair folk's oldest courtesy. A ranger who meets a traveller on the tops, the shepherds say, may offer it, and a traveller who drinks is the family's guest for a night and a day, and a traveller who refuses has insulted the whole family; and a traveller who drinks too much forgets the way home, and is found in the spring dancing in a ring that nobody else can see. Elvinia Dareal of Caer Witrin wants a horn of it for the Feast of the Decadent, and she has not said whether she means to drink it or to learn what is in it.

The ranger is not quick to start a quarrel. Rangers rarely are. They have bows, and time, and a long memory for anyone who takes the family's brew without being offered it.
legend: Tylwyth Teg Ranger, level 46-47, walks alone in the Pennine woods east of the rovers' ground. Aggro level 51, so he often lets you be. Plain melee in the data. Kill one for the Tylwyth Teg brew in Feast of the Decadent and take it to Elvinia Dareal in Caer Witrin. Do not drink it on the way. Respawn five minutes.

aggro: The family will hear of this.
death: The brew... goes back to the woods...

lairEntry: A fair-folk ranger with a horn at the belt.
